layout: Keep the tree: tools/*.py side by side (design.py puts its own directory first on sys.path and imports the others by module name); ROOT = the parent of tools/ (common.ROOT). The files of runtime_files are the import closure of design.py (every module any of them imports, also lazily) plus the two data files; nothing else is read from ROOT on the path of another prefix's pilot (c8-d3).

assemble.vendored() reads ROOT/tools/VENDORED.json and executes ROOT/vendor/c8_assembly/order8_assembly.py from the very bytes whose sha256 equals the pin there (2127196f...: your own H2 file; W23's class, Stage-6 fix round 4: compiled from the verified bytes, never re-read through the import system).

A pilot of THIS package (prefix c8-d2) is verified by production.verify_base against ROOT/inputs/, the pinned tools and the vendored-assembly pins of its inputs manifest, so it needs the whole C62d package; the vendored subset serves pilots of another prefix (yours, c8-d3), which are read through the campaign interface only.

Python >= 3.10 with numpy and scipy (scipy.special.gammaln in the P8 penalty and scipy.stats kurtosis/skew in report; production.py imports scipy.stats.qmc only in plan code). Tested here with numpy 1.23.5 / scipy 1.10.0 (Mac, Python 3.10.11) and before with numpy 2.3.5 / scipy 1.17.0 (symmetry venv: the pilot, production and J-DES-5 jobs). External commands: sacct and scontrol (tools/accounting.py, only when a checkpoint of the pilot carries a Slurm id; see input_interface.eta_node_paths).

schema_prefix_rule.not_prefixed: the route-(b) gate record schema c8-d2-numerics-flags-1 and the build-binding/gate-inputs schemas (route (b) is refused for any prefix but c8-d2)
schema_prefix_rule.rule: the prefix names the pilot campaign's own schema; a ledger record of another prefix is refused (freeze/report exit 2, accounting.py exit 2, ledger.py exit 64), never skipped. A c8-d3 campaign is accounted from its own c8-d3-ledger-1 ledger. A c8-d2 plan refuses a bundle of another prefix; design.read_bundle reads a bundle only under the prefix given.

input_interface.how_a_foreign_pilot_is_read: For prefix != c8-d2, design.py reads the campaign through this interface only (no verify_base): the manifest, the group configs at their manifest pins, validated merged tables, its own ledger and checkpoints (eta_node), and the inputs you pass, which must be the files the pilot's inputs manifest lists. Unchanged since the previous issue except where a field says "since".

fields_read: seed, executable_sha256, numerics, rates_identity, inputs_manifest_sha256, test_only, backend, threads, allocation: REQUIRED, copied into the bundle's pilot record (a missing key is a KeyError, exit 1); numerics and rates_identity must also equal every merged.json's; rates_identity "default" unless freeze --rates-bundle; test_only true allows only --test-only bundles
jobs[] {group, shard, blocks}: the checkpoint scan of eta_node (accounting.checkpoint_ids, missing_checkpoints)
RUN/manifest.json.manifest_sha256: sha256 of the file bytes (every merged.json must name it)

RUN/groups/<name>/config.json.read_at: the manifest's groups[].sha256 pin (common.read_verified: parsed from the digested bytes)
fields_read: counts {graph id as string: points per replicate} (the graphs of the group)
RUN/groups/<name>/config.json.config_hash: object_hash(config) = sha256 of json.dumps(config, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)

checks: sector, L, campaign equal the config
rates_identity and numerics equal the manifest's (both REQUIRED in merged.json)
graph_replicates_sha256, graph_tails_sha256, graph_costs_sha256 == sha256 of the three CSV files
fields_used: row_seconds_sum and thread_seconds_sum: eta_omp,g = row_seconds_sum / thread_seconds_sum, capped at 1 (1.0 when thread_seconds_sum is 0 or absent; row_seconds_sum is REQUIRED when thread_seconds_sum is present)
thread_seconds_sum (accounting: busy thread-seconds; REQUIRED when eta_node comes from accounting.py)

RUN/groups/<name>/graph_replicates.csv.header: replicate,graph,jet_0,...,jet_{2(9-L)-1} (the first line is skipped unread)
RUN/groups/<name>/graph_replicates.csv.rows: one per (replicate, graph) for EVERY graph of config.counts and every replicate 0..replicates-1: the jets of that graph summed over its points (floats as text). design.py does not check completeness (a missing row stays 0 and biases sigma); a graph not in config.counts is a KeyError
RUN/groups/<name>/graph_replicates.csv.use: sigma_g^2 = n_g Var_rep(J_8 . jet_g) at the pilot means; the pilot means (equal-weight campaigns); report statistics; rates rule

RUN/groups/<name>/graph_costs.csv.header: read with csv.DictReader: columns graph and row_seconds (any other column ignored; yours, graph,points,row_seconds,tasks, fits)
RUN/groups/<name>/graph_costs.csv.use: c_g = row_seconds / (replicates x points per replicate); a graph without a row gets the cost floor 1e-12

RUN/groups/<name>/graph_tails.csv.header: read with csv.DictReader: graph, points, tail_n, tail_sum, top_1..top_<tail_n> (|t| descending; the column names are top_<i>, not tail_top_<i>); the replicate column is not read
RUN/groups/<name>/graph_tails.csv.rows: one per (replicate, graph); a graph's rows are taken in file order, and a graph with fewer rows than replicates is "undefined"
RUN/groups/<name>/graph_tails.csv.use: the Hill xi, largest share, screen/confirm (L8 only), undefined reasons (report)

RUN/submissions.jsonl.schema: <prefix>-ledger-1 (one JSON object per line; blank lines skipped)
RUN/submissions.jsonl.read_by: design.eta_node (ledger.read: the schema of every record, also with --eta-node) and tools/accounting.py account() (ledger.jobs and the attempt evidence)
fields_read: schema (every line; another prefix is refused, never skipped)
type: "note" and "attempt" lines are not jobs (an attempt line still raises the number of sacct attempts required for its jobid)
jobid (as a string; the first non-note record of a jobid gives its role)

role: lane, array or sweep are the WORK roles (the eta_node denominator); plan, merge or anything else is overhead. ledger.py register accepts only sweep|plan|lane|array|merge; a record written directly with another role (e.g. pilot_lane) counts as overhead, not work
restart_count (string or int; the attempts that sacct --duplicates must show = max restart_count + 1)
array (role array only: the element spec, e.g. "0-3,7%2")
RUN/submissions.jsonl.not_read: time, source, host, partition, cpus_on_node, account, note
RUN/submissions.jsonl.written_by: C62d: tools/slurm_submit.py, or ledger.py register RUN --role sweep|plan|lane|array|merge --job ID [--restart N] --schema-prefix P (under the campaign lock)

submissions_jsonl_optionality.summary: OPTIONAL only for a --test-only freeze or report whose pilot checkpoints carry no Slurm id (or that passes --eta-node): then design.py reads the file only if it exists (an absent file is an empty ledger) and assumes eta_node 1.0 (or takes --eta-node). REQUIRED for every non-test (production) freeze or report, and for any design whose checkpoints carry Slurm ids: every Slurm job a checkpoint names must be a ledger job, else "allocation unknown" (exit 2).
eta_node_paths: --eta-node X: --test-only only (else refused); the ledger is still read (schema check), nothing else; eta_node = X

non-test: every checkpoint of every merged group (manifest jobs[] x blocks, groups/<group>/checkpoints/s<shard:06d>_p<part:06d>.json) must exist (Y9: else refused "checkpoint(s) of the merged pilot are missing"), every checkpoint must carry a Slurm id (else refused "no Slurm id"), and accounting.py must be complete (below); there is no assumed or overridden efficiency (Y9)
--test-only without Slurm ids in any checkpoint (or with no checkpoint files at all): eta_node 1.0 "assumed" (missing checkpoints are not checked)
--test-only with Slurm ids: as non-test from accounting.py, except that checkpoints without an id are tolerated

accounting.py (both): every checkpoint's Slurm job in the ledger; one sacct -X --duplicates -n -P -j <ledger jobids> -o JobIDRaw,JobID,ElapsedRaw,AllocCPUS,NodeList,State,Partition (7 fields, integer ElapsedRaw and AllocCPUS); scontrol show node <first node> for ThreadsPerCore when ElapsedRaw > 0; complete only when every line parses, every ledger job (and array element) has as many records as the attempts recorded, every current attempt is terminal (X15) and no checkpoint of a merged group is missing (Y9); eta_node = busy thread-seconds (sum of merged.json thread_seconds_sum) / allocated core-seconds of the work roles (ElapsedRaw x AllocCPUS / ThreadsPerCore), capped at 1 by design.py. Incomplete accounting refuses freeze and report ("eta_node unavailable").

fields_read: runtime.fingerprint.slurm {SLURM_JOB_ID, SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID, SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID, SLURM_RESTART_COUNT}: production.checkpoint_runtime parses the first "runtime": value within the first 64 KiB of the file (full JSON parse as a fallback); the Slurm job is SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID if set, else SLURM_JOB_ID
RUN/groups/<name>/checkpoints/s<shard:06.rule: only existence and the runtime block are read on design.py's path (every group must be merged; an unmerged group of another prefix makes the accounting incomplete). The runtime block is provenance outside the checkpoint payload digest.

notes: eta_node comes from the pilot's own ledger over the work roles (lane, array, sweep) and is busy thread-seconds / allocated core-seconds (<= 1, capped): a short or tail-heavy job gives a low eta_node and a high allocated cost (J-SWEEP-2: 0.306; the L8 pilot: 0.837; the production batch: 0.983). Your accounting.py's eta_node is the inverse ratio (allocated / busy; design_fallback.py uses 1/max(1, it)); do not feed it to --eta-node unchanged.

With 2 replicates per graph (a sweep), kurtosis, skewness, max|z| and P8 are undefined (None); 8 replicates define them. The sector P8 pools only L8 graph-campaigns at exactly 4,096 points per replicate (a production batch has none: P8 null).

A production batch (or any campaign with large replicates) as --pilot: the target rows are hypothetical designs sized from its replicates and will usually be INFEASIBLE under the default caps (C62d's: 2.49 SE at 600,875 core-h with raised caps); read the tails and strata from it, never a design.
design.py pins the numerics and rates identity of its pilot in the bundle. design.py never plans: the bundle is read by your own plan code.
The tests above need C62d's whole package (fixtures, fake worker); vendoring design.py and its runtime files is enough to run it on your campaigns (self-check in NOTE_C62d_to_C63d_2026-10-08_H6.md).
c63d_must_adapt: Vendor runtime_files as a tree at the listed sha256s (tools/seeds.py is new in the list); check vendor/c8_assembly/order8_assembly.py = your H2 file 2127196f....

Present your merged pilot as a c8-d3 campaign the interface accepts (tests/test_pipeline.py d3_view is a worked example): manifest.json of schema c8-d3-production-1 with dimension 3, order 8, groups[] pins and ALL of seed, executable_sha256, numerics, rates_identity, inputs_manifest_sha256, test_only, backend, threads, allocation, jobs[] {group, shard, blocks}. At your 4fbd1ba (read-only look) the manifest has no rates_identity (add "default"), and merged.json has no rates_identity and no row_seconds_sum (yours has integration_core_seconds = the sum of row seconds): a view must add them and re-make the pins (merged.json config_hash, manifest_sha256, payload_sha256; the manifest's groups[].sha256 if a config changes). A byte copy of your files (the current design_adapter.py) does not satisfy this; design.py would stop with a KeyError (exit 1).
Group configs: schema c8-d3-group-1 with campaign, sector, L, replicates, counts {graph id string: points per replicate}.

Tables: graph_replicates.csv complete (every graph and replicate; yours has the same header); graph_costs.csv with graph and row_seconds (yours fits); graph_tails.csv with graph, points, tail_n, tail_sum, top_1..top_<tail_n>, one row per replicate per graph. At your 4fbd1ba the tail columns are named tail_top_1..tail_top_16: design.py reads top_<i> (a KeyError, exit 1), so the view must rename them (and re-pin graph_tails_sha256 and payload_sha256 in merged.json).

Inputs: --inventory and --two-loop (and --selection when given) at the sha256 your inputs manifest lists under "sha256", that manifest beside --inventory at the manifest's inputs_manifest_sha256. Your view copies inputs/manifest.json, inventory.json and two_loop.json; a --selection must be listed there too.

eta_node, the submissions question: for a NON-test freeze or report the view must contain RUN/submissions.jsonl (c8-d3-ledger-1 records {schema, jobid, role, restart_count, [type], [array]}, one per Slurm job of the pilot: role lane for your lane workers (pilot_lane would count as overhead), merge/plan as overhead) AND the checkpoints of every merged group (groups/<g>/checkpoints/s<shard:06d>_p<part:06d>.json for k < blocks of every manifest job, each with runtime.fingerprint.slurm), and sacct/scontrol must answer for those job ids on the host that runs design.py. Without them only --test-only works (eta_node 1.0 assumed, or --eta-node X with X = busy/allocated, i.e. the inverse of your accounting's ratio), and the bundle is then a test-only bundle (design_meta test_only true). Alternatively write the ledger with tools/ledger.py register RUN --role lane|merge|plan --job ID --restart N --schema-prefix c8-d3 (it refuses another role).
Seeds: pass --seeds-log with your seed log (a c8-d3 log {"seeds": [...]} or a JSON list of integers is read; a missing path is silently empty).
Exit code 1 means an interface gap (traceback), 2 a refusal with its reason; with the fix, report exits 0 with INFEASIBLE rows when the caps cannot be met.

Route (b), --numerics and --numerics-gate are C8(2)-only (refused for c8-d3); R7 rates (design.py rates) assume the c8-d2 default rates a .8 / b .9 in --rule one-step and production.DEFAULT_RATES for --spec, which are not yours (.8 / .7): do not use rates for C8(3).
